source: Written from the Fall 2020 – Spring 2027 CS schedules and the catalog prerequisites. Review each year when the new schedule is posted.
general: Every required core course (CS 149, 159, 227, 240, 261, 327, 345, 361) has run every fall and spring since Fall 2020, so the core sequence can start in either term.
CS 430 and CS 412 ran only in spring through Spring 2022 and have run in both terms since Fall 2022.

Systems electives split by term: CS 432 and CS 450 are fall courses; CS 456 and CS 470 are mostly spring; CS 455 ran in some early falls but only in spring since Spring 2025. Check which options run in the student's remaining terms before choosing one.
CS 452 runs only in fall; CS 412 runs in both terms. A student who needs the algorithms elective in a spring term should plan on CS 412.
Summer CS offerings aren't in this schedule data. Confirm any summer course with the department before building a plan around it.
Spring 2027 is the planned schedule and can change; treat it as likely, not certain.

sequences.title: Information security: CS 457 (fall) → CS 458 (spring)
sequences.advice: Have CS 361 done or in progress and statistics done by the fall the student takes CS 457. CS 482 (spring) also fits in that year.

sequences.title: Robotics and AI: CS 354 (fall) and CS 444 (spring)
sequences.advice: Both need CS 240 and statistics, so finish those by the end of the sophomore year (or the first transfer year) to take CS 354 the next fall and CS 444 the following spring.

sequences.title: Final-year systems elective
sequences.advice: CS 432 and CS 450 are effectively fall courses, and the advising sheet recommends taking the systems elective before the final semester. A student graduating in spring should plan it for the fall before, or pick a spring option (CS 456, or CS 455 / CS 470 when scheduled).

sequences.title: Spring-start transfer students
sequences.advice: The core runs every term, so a spring start doesn't delay the core. It does shift which fall-only electives (CS 354, CS 452, CS 457) line up; check them against the student's last fall at JMU.

robotics.summary: The robotics minor is interdisciplinary and ends with a robotics project. Its CS courses are semester-locked: CS 354 (fall only) is a core option and CS 444 (spring only) is an elective.
robotics.caveat: Course list from the 2016–17 catalog; the current catalog page doesn't list the courses. Confirm current requirements with the coordinator, Nathan Sprague.
